title: Orsen and the Summer
premise: Astrid Pemberton has spent seven years raising her daughter Wren alone in the coastal town of Marrow Bay, hiding the truth about the fire that ended her marriage and nearly took her life. When her estranged family summons her to a reunion where her ex-husband's family will also attend, she persuades Orsen Vale, a quiet carpenter restoring the old lighthouse keeper's cottage, to pose as her boyfriend. The fake date deepens into something real, but Astrid's carefully buried secret—that she survived the fire by leaving her sister behind—threatens to surface when her mother arrives with a box of inherited letters. As Orsen's own grief over his late wife mirrors hers, Astrid must finally forgive herself, confess the truth publicly at the reunion's final dinner, and choose to build a visible, imperfect life with Orsen rather than disappear again.
about_author: Beatrix Hartwell is a former small-town bookseller who writes love stories set in places where everyone knows your name and your worst summer. She lives on the coast with two cats and an unreasonable number of unread paperbacks.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet Astrid closing up Pemberton & Wren, her bookshop, as she counts her safe routines: school runs, inventory, avoiding the harbor road past the burned Hollis house. A letter from her mother arrives demanding attendance at the Pemberton family reunion. Emotional beat: the fragile architecture of avoidance established.

chapters.title: A Man Who Fixes Things
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen sands floorboards in the lighthouse cottage, dodging the town's pity about his widower status. He comes into the bookshop for a book on Victorian joinery and stays for Astrid's dry humor. Wren immediately likes him. Emotional beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's scaffolding.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The reunion details arrive: three days at the family inn, and her former brother-in-law Daniel will be there with his new wife. Panic. Wren asks why they never visit Grandma. Astrid, cornered, blurts to Orsen that she needs a date. Emotional beat: desperation dressed as a joke.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Over coffee, they negotiate the fake relationship: no real names of exes, no questions about scars, one weekend only. Orsen agrees too quickly, surprising himself. His late wife's sister texts him about moving on; he ignores it. Emotional beat: contracts built to prevent exactly what both want.

chapters.title: Packing a Lie
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid packs while Wren interrogates her about Orsen, forcing Astrid to rehearse intimacy she doesn't feel entitled to. Flashback fragment: the night of the fire, smoke, a door she didn't open. She shuts the memory away. Emotional beat: guilt traveling in the suitcase.

chapters.title: Arrival at Hollow Pines
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They drive to the family inn, hands linked for the first time in the car. Astrid's mother Grete greets them with cool appraisal; cousins whisper. Orsen plays his role better than expected, and Astrid realizes she likes being looked at through his eyes. Emotional beat: performance becoming shelter.

chapters.title: Cocktails with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. First family dinner. Daniel toasts 'to those we've lost,' staring at Astrid. Her aunt probes about the shop's finances. Orsen deflects with charm, then catches Astrid's trembling hand under the table. Emotional beat: the past seated at every place setting.

chapters.title: The Orchard Walk
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Escaping the party, they walk the orchard and break their own rules—Orsen mentions his wife Lena died of illness, not accident; Astrid says almost nothing back. He notices her flinch at a struck match someone lights. Emotional beat: asymmetry of honesty, tenderness anyway.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the reunion gala, dancing close, the act dissolves—a real kiss behind the boathouse. Astrid pulls away, terrified not of Orsen but of being known. Wren, sent to find them, beams at their joined hands. Emotional beat: joy arriving like an intruder.

chapters.title: What the Letters Say
chapters.summary: Grete's POV (brief interlude). Grete unpacks a box of her late husband's letters, including correspondence revealing he knew the truth about the fire—and protected Astrid anyway. She decides whether to bring it to light. Emotional beat: a mother weighing mercy against truth.

chapters.title: Home, Changed
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Back in Marrow Bay, the fake relationship quietly continues—dinners, Wren's sleepovers, Orsen finishing the cottage and asking Astrid to help choose paint. Neither calls it anything. Emotional beat: the lie outliving its deadline.

chapters.title: Daniel Comes to Town
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Daniel appears at the bookshop, ostensibly buying a gift, actually warning Astrid that Grete has the letters and that 'the whole story should come out.' He implies Astrid's survival was theft. Emotional beat: blackmail wearing the mask of closure.

chapters.title: The Question He Shouldn't Ask
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen finds Astrid's old newspaper clipping about the fire hidden in her stockroom. That evening he gently asks what really happened; she lies, flatly, and he knows it. He leaves without anger, which is worse. Emotional beat: first true fracture between them.

chapters.title: Wren's Map
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ten-year-old Wren draws a map of 'our family' for school, placing Orsen inside the house lines and a stick figure labeled 'Aunt Ivy' outside, crossed out. Astrid finds it and breaks down. Emotional beat: children see the shape of everything.

chapters.title: Ivy
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Full flashback chapter: the fire at the Hollis house seven years ago. Astrid escaped with Wren through the back; her sister Ivy went back for the dog and never came out. Astrid told everyone—including herself—a different story. Emotional beat: the confession the reader has earned.

chapters.title: Running Out of Summer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen, hurt and honest, tells Astrid he can't love someone who won't let him stand next to her. He gives back the spare key. Meanwhile Grete calls: the letters will be read aloud at the family's end-of-summer gathering unless Astrid comes and tells her version first. Emotional beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: The Empty Shop
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid closes the bookshop for a day—the first time in seven years—and sits with Ivy's photograph and her father's unopened letters, which Grete has mailed to her. She reads them: her father knew, forgave her, and asked her to live loudly. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as permission.

chapters.title: The Gathering at Hollow Pines
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. At the end-of-summer dinner, Grete begins reading the letters aloud before the assembled family. Daniel smirks. Astrid stands, takes the page from her mother's hands, and asks to read the rest herself. Emotional beat: the cliff edge.

chapters.title: Everything I Buried
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax. Astrid confesses the full truth—Ivy, the door, the seven years of penance disguised as safety—to her stunned family and to Orsen, who arrived uninvited after all. Daniel's counterattack collapses when Grete sides with her daughter. Emotional beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Aftermath: Astrid visits Ivy's memorial tree at dawn, speaks to her sister aloud, and lets go of the debt she could never repay. She visits Orsen at the finished cottage, not to apologize but to introduce herself honestly for the first time. Emotional beat: grief and love sharing a doorway.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Cottage
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen shows Astrid the room he built facing the sea—with a shelf already stocked with books from her shop. He asks for nothing except the chance to be visible beside her. Wren paints the door yellow. Emotional beat: home rebuilt on truth instead of routine.

chapters.title: Orsen and the Summer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue. One year later: the bookshop hosts a reading of Ivy's favorite novel; Grete visits; Daniel sends a stiff, civil card. Astrid and Orsen walk the harbor road she once avoided, unhurried. Final line lands on the theme: surviving was the price; living is the inheritance. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
